linux.fallback: configured shares as written, not live nfsd/smbd state; Samba registry backend, include= files and usershares are not read (constrained token); a symlinked config file or exports.d is refused
linux.mechanism: bounded no-follow reads of /etc/exports, /etc/exports.d/*.exports and /etc/samba/smb.conf (pure parsers); one lstat of the usershares directory

macos.fallback: not read yet: one unsupported status row, macos:planned

windows.fallback: live Server-service state, not the LanmanServer registry: a stopped Server service is unavailable (windows:shares:netshareenum:server_not_started, or windows:shares:netshareenum:server_unavailable when its RPC endpoint does not answer); STYPE_SPECIAL shares (ADMIN$, C$, IPC$) are flagged special, never hidden, and any other share whose name ends in $ is flagged hidden; access and anonymous are -, ACLs and level 502 are never read
windows.mechanism: NetShareEnum level 2 (netapi32); level 1 (names, no paths) when level 2 is refused

caveats: **Configured, not live; some Samba scope is not read.** Linux reports what the files say, not whether `nfsd` or `smbd` runs or what a client sees. The Samba registry backend, `include =` files and usershares are reported as `constrained` tokens, never as a wrong share list, and `[global]` parameters written after a share section apply to it here but not in Samba.

**The access flags are approximations of the written configuration.** The SMB anonymous flag reflects `guest ok` alone, and `mixed` uses a read or write list only as a presence test, never reading its names. Share names and paths can identify people (Samba `[homes]` and per-user shares), so dispatch is gated at `Infrastructure:Read`.

**Windows is measured under LocalSystem only; macOS is planned.** The Windows leg reads the live state of the Server service through `NetShareEnum`, not the `LanmanServer` registry configuration, and it never reads level 502 (ACLs) or the share remark. It was run natively on kingsley on 2026-10-27 as LocalSystem (elevated): level 2 answered and the administrative shares were flagged `special`. Still unmeasured: the level-1 fallback under a non-admin service identity (the contract predicts it under `NT SERVICE\YuzuAgent`) and the exact status of a stopped Server service, which are taken from the API contract. Paging has not been exercised: the capture host publishes three shares, so no enumeration spanning more than one page has been observed, and the 64 KiB size asked for is a request the service may not honour. `totalentries` is documented as a hint, so `inconsistent_drain` on a stable multi-page host is an unmeasured false-positive risk (the rows are kept; only the status is `constrained`). The macOS share-point and `/etc/exports` read is not implemented; that leg reports one `unsupported` row, `macos:planned`.

definitions.description: Reports the shares this host serves over SMB and NFS: name, path, ro/rw/mixed, whether anonymous access is configured and a few flags, never ACLs or NFS client host lists (clients are a count). On Linux, read from /etc/exports, /etc/exports.d and /etc/samba/smb.conf as written, not live nfsd/smbd state; the Samba registry backend, include files and usershares are not read. On Windows, read live from the Server service through NetShareEnum: the administrative ADMIN$, C$ and IPC$ shares are flagged special, any other share whose name ends in $ is flagged hidden, and a stopped Server service is reported as unavailable, never as an empty list. Under a service identity that is not an administrator (the intended NT SERVICE\YuzuAgent) the Windows leg is predicted (per the NetShareEnum contract; not yet measured) to answer names and kind only, constrained with windows:shares:netshareenum:level2_permission_denied; per that contract, membership of Administrators or Power Users for that identity would restore paths (Server Operators exists only on a domain controller; Windows Server 2022 lists Administrators or Access Control Assistance Operators). The macOS leg is planned and not yet read. A refused or failed read is permission_denied or constrained with a reason token, never an empty result; one source row per source says whether it was read. Share names and paths can embed account names, so the result is sensitive. A leading status row states whether the read was complete.

description: Shares this host serves over SMB/NFS: names, paths and a few flags, never ACLs
how_it_works:
`list` reports the shares this host serves over SMB and NFS: for each, the name, the path, read-only or read-write, whether anonymous access is configured, and a few flags. It changes nothing. On Linux it reads three kinds of local configuration file, so the answer is what the files declare, not what `nfsd` or `smbd` is serving right now; on Windows it asks the Server service what it publishes now (below). Rows come in a fixed order. A `status` row comes first and says whether the read was complete. One `source` row follows for each source the leg knows about (`exports`, `exports_d`, `smb_conf` on Linux; `netshareenum` on Windows), saying `read`, `absent`, `refused` or `failed`, so zero `share` rows is never an ambiguous empty success. The `share` rows come last. On Linux the leg reads `/etc/exports`, the `/etc/exports.d/*.exports` snippets and `/etc/samba/smb.conf` with bounded reads that never follow a symlink at the final path component (a symlinked ancestor directory is followed), under one row and byte budget for the whole listing. Exports lines follow the `exports(5)` grammar. `smb.conf` is read the way Samba reads it in the main: lines before the first `[header]` belong to `[global]`, parameter synonyms collapse to one key so the last occurrence wins, a share that sets nothing itself inherits through its `copy =` chain, then `[global]`, then Samba's built-in defaults. One known difference is in caveat 1. Access control lists, `valid users` and NFS client host lists are never read into a row; an NFS export carries a client count and an anonymous flag only. These rows are not the mapped-drive and session observations `echo` records for `mapdrive`, which track mapped shares in both directions (shares this host maps and sessions into its own shares), not the exports it is configured to offer.

On Windows the leg asks the Server service what it publishes now, through `NetShareEnum` level 2 (name, path, type) from `netapi32`, a page at a time: each call asks for at most 64 KiB (never `MAX_PREFERRED_LENGTH`; the size is a request, not a guarantee), one page is converted at a time and freed before the next, and every entry is charged against the same row and byte budget before it is kept, so memory held is the page the service returns plus the budgeted rows. That bounds memory, not time: the `NetShareEnum` call itself has no deadline, so a wedged (not stopped) Server service holds the dispatch worker until it answers (#3925). Each Windows row carries exactly one kind flag (`disk`, `print`, `device`, `ipc`, or `other` for any other type), then `special` for an administrative share (`ADMIN$`, `C$`, `IPC$`: flagged, never hidden) or `hidden` for any other share whose name ends in `$` (the Windows convention for a share that is not browsable, the meaning `hidden` carries on Linux for `browseable = no`), and `temporary` when the share is temporary. Access and anonymous are `-`: share-level permissions are not read, and neither are ACLs (level 502) or the share remark. If level 2 is refused with `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` the leg retries level 1 (names and kind, no paths) and reports `constrained`; refused at both levels is `permission_denied`. A stopped Server service is reported as `unsupported` with a named token, never as an empty list. Any other failure on any page, or an enumeration that returns `ERROR_MORE_DATA` without a share it has not already returned, discards the rows gathered so far: a partial list is never reported as a complete one. The enumeration is not a snapshot: the service pages by position in its live share list, so a share created or deleted while the leg is reading can be skipped or repeated. A share name returned twice (compared without regard to ASCII case) is kept once, and a multi-page enumeration that ends with a different number of shares than the first page announced is `constrained` with `windows:shares:netshareenum:inconsistent_drain`, the rows kept.

### What you can decide with it

| Question | Where the answer is | What to know |
|---|---|---|
| Which SMB shares does this host offer, and where do they point? | `share` rows with proto `smb`: name, path, `ro`/`rw` | Includes `[homes]`, `[printers]` and `print$` (flagged `special`); a `hidden` flag means `browseable = no` |
| Which NFS paths does this host export, and to how many clients? | `share` rows with proto `nfs`: path, `ro`/`rw`/`mixed`, `clients_<n>` | Client names are never listed, only the count; `mixed` means the client specs disagree on ro or rw |
| Does anything look open to everyone? | The anonymous column | NFS: any client spec of `*`, an empty client or an all-zero network mask. SMB: only `guest ok = yes` as written; whether a client can really connect as guest also depends on `map to guest` and `security` |
| Is root exposed on an NFS export? | The `no_root_squash` flag | Set when neither `root_squash` nor `all_squash` is in effect for some client spec |
| Is the picture complete? | The leading `status` row and the `source` rows | Any `constrained` token names what was not read (a Samba registry backend, an `include =`, usershares, a refused or oversized file) |

On macOS you get nothing: one `unsupported` status row and result status `UNAVAILABLE`; on Windows the same shape means the Server service is stopped or its RPC endpoint does not answer. On Linux a `supported` result with no `share` rows means the three files declare no shares; it does not rule out exports added at runtime without touching `/etc/exports`, a Samba instance started with another config file, or a share kept in Samba's registry (the last is flagged). A host with Samba installed commonly reports `constrained` with `usershares_not_read`, because usershares are never listed and the default usershares directory (`/var/lib/samba/usershares`) exists; setting `usershare max shares = 0` in `smb.conf` states they are off and returns `OK`.

### Diagrams

#### How a Samba share value is resolved

Synonyms such as `writable`, `public` and `browsable` are folded into one key first, so the last occurrence wins as in Samba. The `[global]` lookup is against the whole merged file, which is the one place this plugin differs from Samba (caveat 1).

#### How an NFS export line becomes a row

A spec's own options override the line defaults, and each `sec=` flavour inside a spec is judged separately. A line with no client at all is treated as open to everyone with `clients_0`.
name: shares

columns.description: Row shape discriminator (field 0). Values: status, source, share.
columns.name: row_kind

columns.description: status: the literal "list". source: exports, exports_d, smb_conf or netshareenum. share: nfs or smb.
columns.name: field_1

columns.description: status: supported, constrained, permission_denied or unsupported (the planned macOS leg, a stopped Windows Server service, and a leg that threw). source: read, absent, refused or failed (absent is a state, not a failure). share: the SMB share name, or "-" for NFS (identified by path).
columns.name: field_2

columns.description: status: reason token(s) for a non-supported read, "-" when complete; tokens look like linux:shares:exports:permission_denied, linux:shares:smb_conf:registry_backend, windows:shares:netshareenum:server_not_started, macos:planned. source: the number of shares read from it, "-" unless it was read. share: the exported path ("-" when none is set).
columns.name: field_3

columns.description: share: ro, rw, mixed (clients, security flavours or a Samba read/write list disagree with the share default) or "-" when unknown. Windows rows carry `-`: share-level permissions are not read. Not used by the other kinds.
columns.name: field_4

columns.description: share: true when any client may use it (guest, `*`, a wildcard made only of `*`/`?`, or a network with an all-zero mask), false when not, "-" when unknown. For SMB this reflects `guest ok` as written; whether a client can actually connect as guest also depends on global authentication settings (`map to guest`, `security`). Windows rows carry `-`: share-level permissions are not read. Not used by the other kinds.
columns.name: field_5

columns.description: share: comma-separated flags from hidden, unavailable, special, no_root_squash, clients_<n> (the NFS client count; hosts are never listed), or "-"; on Windows exactly one kind (disk, print, device, ipc or other), then special (STYPE_SPECIAL) or hidden (a share that is not special and whose name ends in $), then temporary when set. Not used by the other kinds.
columns.name: field_6

columns.description: share: the source it came from (exports, exports_d, smb_conf or netshareenum). Not used by the other kinds.
columns.name: field_7

outputs_note: Every row is pipe-delimited; field 0 is the row kind, `-` is an absent value, and the first row is always `status|list|<supported\|constrained\|permission_denied\|unsupported>|<reason or ->`. A `source|<exports\|exports_d\|smb_conf\|netshareenum>|<read\|absent\|refused\|failed>|<share count or ->` row follows for every source the leg knows about (Linux three, Windows one, `netshareenum`; the macOS placeholder answers the status row alone; `absent` is a state, not a failure). Each share is `share|<nfs\|smb>|<name or ->|<path or ->|<ro\|rw\|mixed\|->|<true\|false\|->|<flags or ->|<source>`: the name is the SMB share name and `-` for NFS (identified by path), `mixed` means clients, security flavours, or a Samba read/write list disagree with the share default, and the flags are a closed set: `hidden`, `unavailable` (Samba `available = no`), `special` (Samba `[homes]`, `[printers]`, `[print$]`), `no_root_squash` (root is not squashed: no `root_squash` or `all_squash` in effect) and `clients_<n>`; Windows rows add the kind (`disk`, `print`, `device`, `ipc`, `other`, exactly one per row) and `temporary`, use `special` for `STYPE_SPECIAL` administrative shares and `hidden` for any other share whose name ends in `$`. Every free field is scrubbed of NUL and invalid UTF-8, pipe-escaped, and has a backslash folded to `/` and CR or LF folded to a space (so a Windows path reads `C:/Users`).

privileges.grant: None for LocalSystem (an Administrator), so level 2 answers. Under the intended `NT SERVICE\YuzuAgent` identity (non-interactive, in none of those groups) the contract admits only level 1, so every host would answer names and kind only, `CONSTRAINED` with `windows:shares:netshareenum:level2_permission_denied` and paths `-`; `scripts/install-agent-user.ps1` grants nothing for this and `-Check` does not verify it; level 2 under that identity would need it to be a member of Administrators or Power Users (per the contract: on Windows Server 2022 it lists Administrators or Access Control Assistance Operators instead, and Server Operators exists only on a domain controller; not measured here)
privileges.if_refused: `CONSTRAINED` with `windows:shares:netshareenum:level2_permission_denied` and names only, when level 2 returns `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` and level 1 answers; `PERMISSION_DENIED` / partial with `windows:shares:netshareenum:permission_denied` when both are refused
privileges.measured: Measured 2026-10-27 on kingsley (bare-metal Windows 11) as LocalSystem (elevated): level 2 answers, and ADMIN$, C$ and IPC$ are flagged special. Still unmeasured: the level-1 fallback under a non-admin service identity and the exact status of a stopped Server service (caveat 3)
privileges.runs_as: agent service, LocalSystem today (`#1442`; the intended identity is `NT SERVICE\YuzuAgent`). For a non-interactive caller the `NetShareEnum` contract requires Administrators, Power Users, Print Operators or Server Operators at level 2 (on Windows Server 2022: Administrators, Access Control Assistance Operators or Server Operators); level 1 needs no membership

privileges.grant: None: `/etc/exports`, `/etc/exports.d/*.exports` and `/etc/samba/smb.conf` are world-readable (0644) on stock packages. A site that tightens them can grant read access to the agent account, or accept the token
privileges.if_refused: `PERMISSION_DENIED` / partial with `linux:shares:<source>:permission_denied` when a source was refused and none was read, `CONSTRAINED` when another source was read; the source row says `refused`
privileges.measured: Not measured on the `yuzu-agent` account; the sample was captured as `euid 0` in a container
privileges.runs_as: agent daemon, dedicated unprivileged account (`yuzu-agent` on the packaged unit), never root by design (`docs/agent-privilege-model.md`)

result_status.when: every source that exists was read in full; no shares is `supported` with `absent` or `read|0` source rows

Linux: a source could not be read (a symlinked file or `exports.d` (a NixOS-style `/etc`) is refused rather than followed, a FIFO, a file over 256 KiB, a NUL byte, an I/O error; a containerised agent reads the image's `/etc`, not the host's); its source row says `failed` and the other sources are still reported. A refusal (EACCES/EPERM) is `refused`, not `failed` (the `PERMISSION_DENIED` row below)
Linux: more than 64 `exports.d` snippets or 4096 directory entries; the source row stays `read` with the count of shares read, and the excess snippets are cut

Linux: the Samba shares are incomplete by design: a registry backend (`config backend = registry`, `registry shares = yes`), a live `include =` or `config file =`, a `copy =` target that is missing, names `[global]`, is cyclic, over 255 bytes, deeper than 8, defined after the copying share or re-opened after it (Samba snapshots a copy target where the directive stands; any `copy` line counts, not only the last, and a flagged copying share is still listed, with inherited values that may differ from what Samba applies), or usershares (configured, or the default usershares directory exists and `usershare max shares` is not `0`). A stock Debian host has a compiled-in usershare default the file does not show, so with `usershare max shares` unset and the directory present it lands here, because usershares may be in use and are not listed; `usershare max shares = 0` states they are off and gives `OK`, whatever `usershare path` says

Linux: `usershare max shares` is unset and an `lstat` of the default usershares directory failed for a reason other than absence (for example a permission error), so whether usershares are in use is unknown

more than 512 shares or 1 MiB of share text (name, path and flags, plus a fixed 64-byte charge per share) before pipe-escaping across all sources (the listing stops there; the wire can be up to about twice that), or a name or path over 4096 bytes was cut
a source was refused and no source was read; accumulated constrained tokens may follow, comma-joined
Windows: level 2 returned `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` and level 1 answered; names and kinds only, every path `-`

Windows: a page failed with another `NET_API_STATUS` (`<n>`, decimal), or `ERROR_MORE_DATA` arrived with no share not already returned (no entries, or only names seen before); the source row says `failed` and no share rows are reported, even if earlier pages were read

Windows: a multi-page enumeration finished with a different number of shares than the first page announced, so a share created or deleted while it ran may be missing or repeated, or the first page's `totalentries` (documented as a hint, not a guarantee) disagreed with the count read; the rows are kept and the source row says `read` with the count
Windows: the same budget as Linux (512 shares, 1 MiB, 4096 bytes per name or path); the listing stops at the first share the budget refuses
Windows: `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` at level 2 and again at level 1; source row `refused`

Windows: the Server service is stopped (`NERR_ServerNotStarted`) or its RPC endpoint does not answer (`RPC_S_SERVER_UNAVAILABLE`, `RPC_S_UNKNOWN_IF`); one `unsupported` status row and a `failed` source row, never an empty list
a leg threw: an `unsupported` status row, reported instead of unwinding across the plugin boundary

where_the_data_goes: **Instruction result.** Rows travel over the agent's mTLS gRPC channel as the command response and land in the ResponseStore, queryable at `/api/responses/{id}`. `list` is also a gathered definition (`crossplatform.network.shares`, 3600s TTL).
**Not consumed by** daily-sync, Echo, DEX, or metrics.

**Default on, and how to turn it off.** The plugin is on by default; disable it with the generic per-plugin kill switch (`PUT /api/v1/plugin-config/shares/kill-switch`) or by omitting it from `--plugin-allowlist`.

**Sensitivity.** Share names and paths can embed account names: Samba `[homes]`, per-user shares and Windows user-profile paths. Treat the result as sensitive; dispatch is gated at `Infrastructure:Read` and the stored result is readable by `Response:Read` holders, as for every plugin. No ACLs, `valid users` lists or NFS client host lists are read into a row; NFS clients are a count and an anonymous flag.
**Siblings:** `echo` `mapdrive` (the mapped drives and sessions this host makes and receives, not the exports it offers) and `network_config`.
